intro: The India e-Transit visa is for travelling through India on the way to another country, for example a stopover where you leave the airport. We’ll check whether you need one at all.
cardText: For passing through India on the way to another country. Valid for 30 days.

rules.title: How long you can stay
rules.text: The visa is valid for 30 days from your first arrival.

rules.title: It can’t be extended or changed
rules.text: An e-Visa can’t be extended or switched to another type of visa once you’re in India, so choose the right one before you travel.

rules.title: Arrive at an approved airport or seaport
rules.text: You must enter India through one of the airports or seaports approved for e-Visas. All the main international airports are included, such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Goa and Kochi. You can leave from any immigration checkpoint.

rules.title: Who can’t use an e-Visa
rules.text: People of Pakistani origin, anyone with a military, police or security background (serving or retired), and holders of diplomatic or official passports must apply for a regular visa instead.

rules.title: Fill in the e-Arrival card
rules.text: Before you fly, complete India’s free e-Arrival card online within 72 hours of arrival. It’s arrival information, not a visa. [How the e-Arrival card works](/india-e-arrival-card/)

rules.title: No protected areas
rules.text: An e-Visa isn’t valid for protected, restricted or cantonment areas. Visiting places such as parts of the North East, Sikkim or the Andaman Islands may need a separate permit.

boxText: Pakistani origin, a military or police background, work, journalism or a longer stay all need a regular visa. We help with those too.

sections.heading: Do I need an India e-Transit visa?
sections.text: If you stay airside during a connection and don’t pass through immigration, you may not need a visa. If you leave the airport, change airports or stay overnight outside the airport, you need an e-Transit visa or another visa. Tell us your route and we’ll check.

sections.heading: What you need for an India e-Transit visa
sections.text: Your passport, a recent photo, your confirmed ticket into India and your onward ticket, and a visa for your final destination if that country needs one. Your India e-Transit visa is valid for 30 days from your first arrival.

faqs.q: Do I need an e-Transit visa for a flight connection in India?
faqs.a: Not usually, if you stay airside and don’t go through immigration. If you’ll leave the airport, you need one.
At least 4 days before you arrive in India, and no more than 120 days before. We recommend applying 2 to 3 weeks ahead in case anything needs correcting.

faqs.q: Is the e-Visa fee refundable if I’m refused?
faqs.a: No. The Government of India’s e-Visa fee pays for processing your application, so it isn’t refunded if the visa is refused or you cancel your trip. That’s why we check everything before you pay it.
